findings.claim: The new `ContainsKey` guards turn a duplicate `[Key]` into silent first-wins with no diagnostic. Example input: a `[MessagePackObject]` with `[Key(0)] public int FirstValue` and `[Key(0)] public int SecondValue`, or the same string key on two members. On base, `Dictionary.Add` threw, so the problem surfaced as AD0001 or CS8785. On head nothing is reported. With generation not suppressed, the generated formatter serializes only `FirstValue` and silently drops `SecondValue`, so data is lost on round-trip. The dynamic resolver rejects duplicate keys at run time, so the analyzer now hides an error it used to surface. This also changes behaviour when `SuppressSourceGeneration` is unset, which the requirement says must not change.

receipt_plan.detail: Run Receipts.GeneratedTests.DuplicateKeySilentlyDroppedTests (DuplicateIntKey_IsReportedOrBothMembersSerialized and DuplicateStringKey_IsReportedOrBothMembersSerialized). On head no error, AD0001, CS8785 or generator exception is produced, and the generated code never references SecondValue.

findings.claim: The same silent first-wins guard was added to the string-key path in the second member-collection loop (the field/constructor variant at the 1145-1180 region). A duplicate string key there is dropped without any diagnostic. In map mode the later member, for example a derived `new` member that hides a base member with the same key, is silently not serialized, depending on member enumeration order.

receipt_plan.detail: Same harness as DuplicateStringKey_IsReportedOrBothMembersSerialized, but declare two public fields with [Key("a")]. Assert that a diagnostic is reported or that both fields appear in the generated formatter. On head neither happens.
